item.title: With extremely inappropriate remarks, Mbappé loses trust in the Chinese market on his own
item.description:
Published: 2026-10-27 16:30:00
Kylian Mbappé Photo: VCG A football star can make hundreds of millions on the pitch, only to lose the trust of an entire market by failing to show the most basic respect. French football star Kylian Mbappé has recently sparked a fierce backlash in China after making extremely inappropriate remarks in a recent interview. What did he say? Many Chinese would rather not repeat it. Dongqiudi, a major Chinese football news and community platform, issued a statement saying that it would not translate the interview because the footballer's remarks had hurt the feelings of Chinese fans and the Chinese people. Brands including Dongpeng Beverage Group and Chinese dairy giant Mengniu promptly terminated their cooperation. This is not an emotional outburst, but a rational choice made spontaneously by the market. The message from Chinese consumers is clear: Respect is not optional; one doesn't get to profit from China while disrespecting it. Not a chance. Mbappé's talent and skills are beyond doubt. But talent and public responsibility are two entirely different things. The first determines how many goals you score and how much you are worth; the second determines how many people are still willing to pay for you. Talent may open the door to a market, but respect is what keeps it open. We don't know whether Mbappé would deliberately set out to offend a country whose market has helped fuel his commercial success. One thing is for sure: He lacks cross-cultural awareness, and fails to appreciate the responsibilities that come with global fame. Had he shown even a basic understanding of Chinese culture and sensitivities, he might have thought twice before speaking so disrespectfully. Every culture has its boundaries. That is no secret. No one expects a foreign athlete to be an expert on China. But global superstars who have long profited from commercial partnerships in China should make an effort to understand the country's cultural sensitivities and show a basic level of respect. That is not asking for special treatment. It is basic commercial common sense. For Chinese brands, terminating such cooperation is no small decision. Previous marketing investments, contractual obligations and the cost of replacing promotional materials all mean real costs. Yet, by cutting ties, these companies are sending a clear message: When public sentiment is offended, businesses cannot pretend nothing has happened. China's market remains open and welcomes athletes and brands from around the world to share in its opportunities. But an open market is not a market without boundaries. The threshold is respect. Those who disregard the feelings of the Chinese people should not expect to escape the commercial consequences. For decades, some international public figures have been happy to take the money from the Chinese market while talking carelessly about China. When it comes to matters of principle, they tend to dismiss offensive remarks as "personal expression" or hide behind "freedom of speech." That's no excuse. This time, Mbappé has learned the hard way — and he has only himself to blame. His case should serve as a clear red line for every foreign public figure hoping to profit from China: On issues of national sentiment, no one has the freedom to act recklessly. Going forward, our commercial contracts might as well spell out clearer clauses governing public conduct. The national feelings of the Chinese people are not to be provoked, and the Chinese market will leave no room for those who display arrogance and disrespect.

item.title: China urges Europe to respect market economy after EU eyes broader import restrictions on Chinese chemicals, furniture, and machinery
item.description:
Published: 2026-10-27 16:12:00
Chinese Foreign Ministry spokesperson Guo Jiakun Commenting on reports that the European Union (EU) is s discussing plans to reduce imports of Chinese chemicals, furniture, machinery and other products, Chinese Foreign Ministry spokesperson Guo Jiakun said on Tuesday that the essence of China-EU economic and trade relations lies in mutual benefit and win-win cooperation. China hopes the European side will respect the principles of market economy and fair competition, avoid the abuse of trade remedy tools. "China hopes the European side will respect the principles of market economy and fair competition, avoid the abuse of trade remedy tools, and use concrete actions to promote the healthy and stable development of China-EU relations," Guo said at a regular press conference. According to the spokesperson, the second meeting of the China-EU trade and investment consultation mechanism has made positive progress, which shows that the two sides can fully resolve economic and trade differences properly through dialogue and consultation. Strengthening dialogue and consultation and deepening economic and trade cooperation on the basis of mutual respect is in the common interest of both sides and is also the general expectation of businesses and people in both countries, he added. Global Times

item.title: China's upgraded Jiaolong submersible completes 7,000-meter-class sea trials
item.description:
Published: 2026-10-27 16:11:00
China’s upgraded manned deep-sea submersible Jiaolong is recovered on October 2, 2026, after completing its 465th dive, during which it reached a depth of 7,056.9 meters. Photo: Xinhua China’s upgraded manned deep-sea submersible Jiaolong has successfully completed multiple 7,000-meter-class sea trials in the Philippine Basin, confirming the reliability and safety of the upgraded submersible and its domestically produced key components and strengthening China’s technological edge in manned deep-sea exploration equipment, the Xinhua News Agency reported on Tuesday. The sea trials were conducted as part of the second leg of China’s 100th oceanographic expedition. The submersible completed three test dives in the Philippine Basin, including two dives to depths exceeding 7,000 meters, reaching a maximum depth of 7,056.9 meters. All test parameters met the requirements for 7,000-meter-class sea trials. Sun Yongfu, a researcher at the National Deep Sea Center, said the sea trials fully verified the reliability and safety of Jiaolong following its iterative upgrades and the replacement of key components with domestically produced alternatives, consolidating and enhancing China’s technological advantages in manned deep-sea submersible technology. Before the scientific expedition, the submersible received major upgrades, including a 7,000-meter-class high-energy-density lithium battery pack, domestically developed low-noise DC thrusters and advanced hydraulic and imaging systems. The upgrades introduced technological innovations across key components and systems, including power supply, propulsion, hydraulics, electrical systems, and communication and observation, significantly enhancing the submersible’s operational capabilities. According to Sun, following its upgrades and the localization of key components, submersible conducted multiple scientific missions in different sea areas to investigate deep-sea resources and marine ecosystems. These scientific expeditions will further deepen international cooperation in marine science, significantly advancing China’s deep-sea exploration and research, and contribute to the country’s goal of becoming a maritime power, Sun said. Global Times

item.title: German president kicks off China visit, eyeing dialogue opportunities amid trade tensions
item.description:
Published: 2026-10-27 15:42:00
German President Frank-Walter Steinmeier (front) departs for China on October 26, 2026. Photo: VCG German President Frank-Walter Steinmeier arrived in Hefei, East China's Anhui Province, early Tuesday for a five-day state visit, his first trip to China in nearly eight years, as Berlin and Beijing seek to navigate trade tensions and their increasingly complex relationship. Ahead of the visit, Steinmeier said on social media on Monday that the trip would focus on Germany's multifaceted relationship with China and the challenges facing the two countries. Posting on Instagram, Steinmeier said that in Anhui, the focus will be on China around the turn of the 20th century and the significance of that period for the history of German-Chinese encounters. In the Huangshan Mountains in Anhui, Steinmeier will visit a place closely associated with Chinese art and philosophy that has also inspired European artists and thinkers. In the provincial capital Hefei, the program includes, among other things, a visit to Volkswagen, according to his post. Steinmeier's visit to Volkswagen's facilities in Anhui underscores the importance he attaches to practical industrial cooperation alongside broader strategic dialogue, Jiang Feng, a researcher at Shanghai International Studies University and president of the Shanghai Regional Studies Association, told the Global Times. Volkswagen's operations in Anhui have explored new models of China-Germany cooperation in the automotive sector, including vehicle exports to Europe, he said. Jiang noted that the visit will offer Steinmeier a firsthand look at how such initiatives could help address bilateral trade frictions and open up new avenues for cooperation. The German president said his visit to China includes Anhui and Beijing. In the Chinese capital, the program includes talks with Chinese leaders, as well as a speech at Peking University on China's role in the world. On Friday, Chinese Foreign Ministry spokesperson Mao Ning said during a press conference that the sound and steady growth of the comprehensive strategic partnership between China and Germany, the world's second- and third-largest economies, not only serves the interests of both countries, but is also what Europe and the world hope to see. "We hope to work with the German side to take this visit as an opportunity to cement mutual trust, deepen cooperation and seek joint innovation, so as to make greater progress in bilateral relations, contribute to steady and sustained growth of China-Europe relations, and bring fresh energy to the world," Mao added. China's relations with Germany and the European Union (EU) have reached a point where both sides need to rethink their approach, as trade tensions and diverging strategic perceptions increasingly complicate cooperation, Jiang said. Steinmeier, a longtime advocate of closer ties with China, could use the visit to gain a deeper understanding of the country and encourage German leaders to see China as a strategic partner rather than the source of Europe's problems, Jiang said. The trade disputes between China and the EU, however, do not amount to an insurmountable crisis, he added. The challenge lies in finding new ways to bridge differences and lay the groundwork for stronger China-Germany relations.

item.title: US intelligence hypes Chinese, Russian space threats while accelerating its own military buildup in orbit
item.description:
Published: 2026-10-27 15:08:00
Militarizing space. Illustration: Chen Xia/GT Like Don Quixote tilting at windmills he mistook for menacing giants, Washington appears to be sounding the alarm over alleged threats in outer space, even as it presses ahead with its own military buildup in orbit. In its latest assessment, released on Monday, the US Defense Intelligence Agency (DIA) claimed that China could deploy space-based directed-energy weapons by the late 2020s, while also highlighting Russia's expanding anti-satellite capabilities, according to SpaceNews. The claims come as the US itself accelerates the militarization of outer space, having already publicly acknowledged deploying weapons in orbit while advancing its ambitious Golden Dome missile defense initiative. Chinese military affairs expert Song Zhongping told the Global Times that Washington's approach represents a classic case of "thief crying stop the thief," as the US seeks to justify its own buildup of offensive and defensive space capabilities by portraying China and Russia as growing threats. According to SpaceNews, the DIA's latest assessment, contained in the 2026 edition of Challenges to Security in Space, claimed that China already possesses multiple ground-based laser systems capable of disrupting, degrading or damaging satellites in low-Earth orbit. The report further alleged that Beijing may field space-based directed-energy weapons by the late 2020s, along with more powerful ground-based systems capable of threatening satellites in orbit. Directed-energy weapons use concentrated electromagnetic energy, including lasers and high-powered microwaves, to interfere with or damage targets. Such systems could potentially disrupt satellite electronics or impair optical sensors, according to SpaceNews. The US intelligence report also highlighted Russia's alleged development of kinetic anti-satellite weapons, including the Burevestnik system, which it described as a developmental co-orbital anti-satellite weapon launched from a modified MiG-31 aircraft. It further reiterated Washington's assessment that Moscow is developing a satellite designed to carry a nuclear weapon. Moscow has said that Cosmos 2553, a satellite linked by US intelligence to the alleged program, was intended to test electronic systems under radiation conditions. The latest allegations stand against the backdrop of Washington's increasingly explicit pursuit of military capabilities in space. On September 14, US Secretary of the Air Force Troy Meink publicly acknowledged that the US already possessed on-orbit space control weapons capable of defending its military forces against hostile actions, according to a release on the US Space Force website. The announcement marked a significant development in Washington's public posture toward space warfare, although the US military did not disclose the specific capabilities, the number deployed or their deployment dates. Meanwhile, Washington is pressing ahead with its Golden Dome missile defense initiative, which includes the development of a constellation of space-based interceptors. According to an official US Space Force release in July, the program aims to develop interceptors capable of engaging missiles during their boost, midcourse and glide phases. According to an official US Space Force release in April, the service has established the Space-Based Interceptor (SBI) program to develop a space-based missile defense system, with plans to demonstrate its integration into the Golden Dome architecture by 2028. Song said the latest US intelligence assessment reveals two distinct strategic calculations behind Washington's emphasis on China and Russia. By hyping China's potential development of space-based weapons, the US is seeking to justify its own deployment of offensive weapons in orbit, while exaggerating Russia's anti-satellite capabilities serves to make the case for strengthening the defenses of American space assets, Song said. Such arguments could also help Washington secure additional congressional funding for an integrated space warfare architecture combining offensive and defensive capabilities, he said. Song noted that the US is increasingly seeking to transform outer space from a domain used primarily to support military operations through reconnaissance, communications and navigation into a domain for direct offensive and defensive operations. He said Washington's pursuit of space-based weapons, including capabilities envisioned under the Golden Dome initiative, reflects its broader ambition to maintain military superiority by integrating advanced technologies and extending military operations into space. China, meanwhile, has repeatedly called for efforts to prevent an arms race in outer space and opposed attempts to turn it into a battlefield. In its latest position paper titled China's Position on Strengthening Outer Space Governance, released on October 23, the Chinese Foreign Ministry warned: "The risk of an arms race in outer space and the trend of turning outer space into a new theater of conflict have become the gravest threat and challenge to space security." The document further stated: "States should oppose offensive military policies in outer space and take all possible measures to prevent an arms race in outer space." Song warned that Washington's push to integrate artificial intelligence into military systems and expand offensive and defensive capabilities into space reflects its ambition to maintain military dominance. Such developments could transform outer space from a domain supporting military operations into a battlefield, threatening other countries' space assets and potentially accelerating an arms race and increasing the risk of conflicts triggered by miscalculation, he said.

item.title: Chinese netizens call on Mbappé to apologize as brands cut ties over remarks
item.description:
Published: 2026-10-27 12:27:00
Kylian Mbappé of Real Madrid reacts during the match between FC Barcelona and Real Madrid at Camp Nou in Barcelona, Spain on October 25, 2026. Photo: VCG Chinese netizens have called on French football star Kylian Mbappé to apologize over his erroneous remarks about China in an interview that sparked widespread criticism, as at least three Chinese companies have terminated their cooperation with the Real Madrid forward and media platforms have taken out content related to the footballer. The hashtag #MbappeStillOwesAnApology has gained traction on social media platform Sina Weibo, amid growing calls for the Real Madrid forward to apologize for his remarks about China. "Mbappé is the captain of the French national team and Real Madrid's star player, yet he has shown no respect for other countries' history and great figures. This is deeply disappointing," a Chinese user posted on Sina Weibo, drawing many likes. "If he chose to make such remarks, he must also bear the consequences." Dongpeng Beverage Group announced on Tuesday that it would terminate all cooperation with Mbappé, saying it firmly opposed and had zero tolerance for conduct that hurts national sentiments. "Our company firmly opposes and maintains a zero-tolerance stance toward any actions that hurt the national sentiments of the people. Effective immediately, we are terminating all cooperation with Kylian Mbappé," the company said in a statement. Chinese dairy giant Mengniu also decided to terminate its cooperation with the French forward. "Mengniu firmly opposes and has zero tolerance for any words or actions that hurt the feelings of the Chinese people," the Mengniu statement reads. Cheese-making company Milkground also announced on Tuesday that it would end all cooperation with Mbappé, saying it firmly opposes and has zero tolerance for any words or actions that hurt the feelings of the Chinese people. The commercial fallout came amid a broader response from Chinese media platforms and brands. RedNote, a Chinese social media platform that had a cooperation contract with Mbappé in 2024, said Tuesday that it was reviewing and removing related content and materials. News apps operated by state broadcaster CCTV have also removed content related to the French striker. Sources at China Media Group, CCTV's parent organization, confirmed that the group had suspended broadcasts of matches involving La Liga and Mbappé, Shanghai-based news outlet The Paper reported Tuesday. International brands such as Dior, On and Hublot have also removed their Mbappé-related content on Sina Weibo. Mbappé's accounts on RedNote and Sina Weibo can no longer be followed, with both platforms displaying a notice stating that the accounts have been "muted for violating relevant community rules." The decisions followed mounting criticism on Chinese social media after an interview featuring Mbappé circulated online. The backlash intensified late on Monday, when Dongqiudi, a major Chinese football news and community platform, issued a statement saying that it would not translate the interview because the footballer's remarks had hurt the feelings of Chinese fans and Chinese people. The Dongqiudi statement prompted further criticism of Mbappé, with users questioning his conduct and calling on Real Madrid to address the controversy. One highly upvoted comment questioned why Real Madrid players repeatedly found themselves embroiled in controversies, referring to defender Dean Huijsen's incident involving offensive content about Asians in February and the club's social media post in August referring to flood victims in the Himalayas. The latter wording also drew criticism from Chinese users over the omission of China's name in the reference. Commentary in Chinese media also questioned the conduct of public figures seeking commercial opportunities in China while making remarks perceived as disrespectful to Chinese people. "The Chinese market embraces the world with open arms, welcoming celebrities, athletes, businesses and brands from all countries to share in its development opportunities," Jimu News said in a commentary. However, the outlet argued that the market had no place for "two-faced" figures who abandoned their principles for profit or "opportunists" who spoke recklessly for personal gain. It questioned how anyone could expect to benefit from endorsement deals in China while treating the feelings and beliefs of Chinese people as a joke in interviews. "The greater a football star's influence, the more mindful they should be of their words and actions. Outstanding performances on the pitch do not give anyone the privilege to cross the line without regard for others. Respect must be mutual," Zhu Meng, a Beijing-based sports commentator, told the Global Times. "Once that basic principle is abandoned, even the brightest star power cannot offset the harm caused by their remarks, and they must be prepared to face the consequences." The controversy originated from an interview published by football-focused online show The Bridge . Discussion of an internet meme featuring Mbappé drew criticism in China, where online users questioned the appropriateness of his comments and their implications for Chinese fans.

item.title: Swiss-Italian exhibition in Beijing explores how Italian culture shapes architecture
item.description:
Published: 2026-10-27 11:51:00
Visitors explore the exhibition at the Italian Cultural Institute in Beijing on October 22, 2026. Photos: Dong Feng/Global Times The Embassy of Switzerland in China and the Embassy of the Republic of Italy in China jointly launched an exhibition titled Lingua, Paesaggio, Architettura (or Language, Landscape, Architecture) in Beijing on October 22. As part of the events marking the Week of the Italian Language in the World, the exhibition explores how Italian terms or wordings shape the perception and design of architecture. This exhibition explores how Italian-language terms influence both the understanding of architecture and the practice of architectural design. Through photographs, texts and interviews, the exhibition showcases a selection of architectural and landscape concepts from Italian-speaking communities who are based in Switzerland, including case studies of square, landscape and garden from the Ticino region, which is the southernmost, exclusively Italian-speaking canton of Switzerland. Krystyna Marty Lang, Ambassador of Switzerland to China, delivers a speech at the exhibition inauguration in Beijing on October 22, 2026. Krystyna Marty Lang, Ambassador of Switzerland to China, said that Switzerland is characterized by its linguistic and cultural diversity; language serves not merely as a tool for communication, but also as a force that shapes cognition and modes of thought. This exhibition aims to establish a platform for dialogue among Switzerland, Italy, and China. Cultural exchange, in this context, centers around mutual listening, reciprocal learning, and stimulating creativity, rather than serving as a one-way presentation, noted Lang. Ambassador Lang said it is expected that the exhibition will inspire audiences of diverse professional backgrounds and nationalities to engage in new forms of exchange and dialogue. Felix Schwendimann, counselor and head of Culture and Media at the Embassy of Switzerland in China, told the Global Times that with its various working languages, Switzerland places great value on cultural diversity. Through the events, the embassy seeks to further highlight its unique cultural character and foster interaction among language enthusiasts. Minister Cristina Carenza, deputy head of mission of the Embassy of the Republic of Italy in China, delivers a speech at the inauguration ceremony on October 22, 2026. Minister Cristina Carenza, deputy head of mission of the Embassy of the Republic of Italy in China, said that the exhibition allows visitors to interpret architecture from three distinct perspectives: Swiss, Italian, and Chinese. The exhibition enables mutual learning among different civilizations and cultures; through the specialized vocabulary of architecture, which embodies years of historical practice and accumulated knowledge, visitors can collectively conceive, design, and create spaces, said Carenza. Swiss curator Christian Herren, said that while preparing for this exhibition he has interviewed Chinese architects who studied at the Accademia di architettura di Mendrisio , the architecture faculty of the Università della Svizzera italiana located in Mendrisio, Switzerland. By examining the differing cultural connotations of everyday settings - such as hutongs (Beijing's traditional alleys, an enduring symbol of the capital's culture and history) and public squares - across various languages, the discussion highlights the variations in spatial cognition that underlie these terms. Herren specifically mentioned that Chinese architect Li Yaoming had suggested translating hutong into Italian as vicolo . However, the Italian word does not fully capture the vibrant, lived-in atmosphere of hutongs . Italian architect and designer Fabrizio Gurrado explored how language shapes the way people perceive and understand space, places, and man-made environments, while also examining Italian architectural styles and their contemporary manifestations. In particular, Gurrado, who worked in China for 13 years, shared how the design style of Andrea Palladio, one of the most influential architects of the Italian Renaissance, influenced the Tsinghua University Art Museum. The exhibition will continue at the Italian Cultural Institute in Beijing until November 22.

item.title: Why has the CPC succeeded? The fifth plenary session provides a window of observation: Global Times editorial
item.description:
Published: 2026-10-27 00:51:00
The view of Beijing's Central Business District Photo: VCG How has this massive party of unprecedented scale demonstrated formidable organizational mobilization and implementation capacity when confronted with major risks and challenges? When the international community turns its attention to the fifth plenary session, it is not just observing China's politics; more importantly, it seeks insights from "China's governance" for political party building, national governance across the world, and even the reform of the global governance system. The 20th Central Committee of the Communist Party of China (CPC) is holding its fifth plenary session in Beijing from October 26 to 29 to deliberate on major issues concerning the continued advancement of full and rigorous Party self-governance. Marking the 105th anniversary of the founding of the CPC and the launch year of the 15th Five-Year Plan, this plenary session draws global attention to the underlying foundations of China's development. Particularly against the backdrop of partisan politics in many countries being mired in polarized, fragmented and chaotic contests, with many ruling parties feeling helpless in the face of social division and stalled development at home, why does China present a completely different picture? The fifth plenary session serves as an important window for the world to gain insights. For anyone following China, today's China is defined not merely by economic growth, technological breakthroughs and landmark projects. The robust organizational capacity and political strength underpinning these remarkable achievements further illuminate the source of China's steady progress amid profound changes of the times. As the largest governing party in the world, the CPC maintains solidarity and unity at all times. How has this massive party of unprecedented scale demonstrated formidable organizational mobilization and implementation capacity when confronted with major risks and challenges? When the international community turns its attention to the fifth plenary session, it is not just observing China's politics; more importantly, it seeks insights from "China's governance" for political party building, national governance across the world, and even the reform of the global governance system. An increasing number of insightful observers around the world have identified a clear thread running through China's development: The leadership of the CPC has consistently served as the central pillar underpinning the steady advancement of the country's various undertakings and is the master key to unlocking the secret behind the success of "the governance of China." Persistently advancing full and rigorous Party self-governance constitutes the fundamental mechanism at the heart of this master key. Since the 18th CPC National Congress, the great new project of Party building in the new era has been advanced in depth. China has continuously intensified its fight against corruption, improved its intra-Party oversight system, and made sustained efforts to enhance Party conduct through regular and long-term mechanisms. These efforts have included combating formalism and bureaucratism, holding officials accountable for dereliction of duty and failure to fulfill their responsibilities, and encouraging officials to take initiative and fulfill their duties. Such measures have helped ensure that decisions and plans made by the central leadership are effectively implemented at all levels and that resources and efforts from across society remain consistently directed toward shared goals. This political courage to turn the blade inward and confront problems within the Party itself is rarely seen in the history of political parties worldwide. For a long time, many voices in international public discourse have taken it for granted that there are only a handful of established models for building a governing party, as though effective governance could be achieved only by replicating certain institutional frameworks. China has challenged these conventional assumptions with verifiable development data. One of the most tangible outcomes of these measures is that public trust in the ruling party in China has remained consistently high for many years. Meanwhile, the efficiency with which major national strategies are implemented and the continuity of public policy execution have gained widespread international recognition. The principle that the governance over the Party must precede the governance of the country is grounded in concrete and profound practical realities. In today's international community, a stark contrast has emerged between "China's governance" and "the West's chaos." Some Western countries that firmly believe in multiparty systems and the separation of powers are mired in intensified partisan conflicts and frequent changes of government. Internal political polarization is escalating, societal divisions are deepening, and public policies fluctuate under the tug-of-war of interest groups, making it difficult to reach consensus even on basic livelihood issues. Some Western scholars, after comparing the party politics of major powers, have had to admit that "the CPC possesses strong governing capacity." In recent years, party representatives from various regions, including Southeast Asia, Africa, Europe, and Latin America, have come to China to study and learn from the governance experiences of the CPC through inter-party exchanges. China's long-term approach to development, strategic vision, and practical achievements have opened up broader intellectual space for countries to independently explore political development paths that align with their own national conditions. The world today needs truly effective governance solutions more than ever. An increasing number of countries and political parties are drawing inspiration from "China's governance" to explore governance paths that suit their own national situations. This not only provides more diverse practical solutions for the global governance system but also strengthens the consensus among countries to collectively address global challenges. It is also the precious public value contributed by China through its unwavering efforts to promote full and rigorous Party self-governance amid a world marked by intertwined changes and turmoil.

item.title: GT Voice: Rare-earth metal recycling should not be driven by geopolitics
item.description:
Published: 2026-10-26 22:05:00
Rare earth File photo:VCG An American recycling company is recovering rare-earth metals from old wind turbines, which The Wall Street Journal said over the weekend could be one part of a drive to help reduce US reliance on China for the materials. While recycling critical materials from retired equipment can tap existing resources, treating rare-earth magnet recycling as a breakthrough to achieve critical minerals "self-sufficiency" or framing it as a shortcut to shake off reliance on China's supply chain, seriously underestimates industrial realities. Rare-earth metals are widely used in wind power systems, new-energy vehicles and high-end manufacturing, serving as core components of the modern industrial system. As these industries expand, recycling materials from old equipment has broad long-term potential. But being technically recoverable is not the same as being commercially viable and capable of stable industrial supply. The disassembly, separation and purification of wind turbines involve highly complex processes, which place high demands on specialized equipment, technical expertise and environmental protection treatment. Once transportation, labor and processing costs are added up, whether recycled products can compete with existing supplies on price and quality still has to be tested by the market. An even trickier hurdle lies in the stability of the feedstock. Wind turbines are generally engineered for service lives of more than two decades. Most large-scale wind farms installed across Europe and the US came online only in the past decade, so very few turbines have reached retirement age. Even if some turbines are replaced with better models, recyclers may still face uneven, scattered and non-standardized feedstock. Without reliable raw material inflows, downstream separation and refining lines cannot run at full capacity, economies of scale remain out of reach, and unit costs stay high. This means recycling can serve as a valuable supplement to critical mineral supplies, but it cannot replace mature supply chains any time soon. In recent years, some Western countries have repeatedly discussed critical mineral security and rolled out multiple policy initiatives, but actual progress has been relatively limited. The problem is not a lack of political will but the fact that building industrial chains follows its own logic. The global supply of critical minerals is never an isolated contest over a single link or a single technology. It is a systemic ecosystem integrating resources, technical expertise, cost control, skilled talent, specialized equipment and downstream market support. Mine development involves long investment cycles, separation and purification pose high technical barriers, and downstream manufacturing requires decades of accumulated experience. A shortfall in any single link will drag down the entire industrial chain. Recycling and refining are never simple matters of technological breakthroughs. The chain equally requires a complete process system, stable raw material supply and a sustainable business model, all of which are necessary. Treating recycling as a shortcut to bypass existing mature supply chains underestimates the systemic difficulty of industrial chain construction. China's rare-earth industry took shape over decades of steady accumulation. Yet today, some economies enjoy the benefits of the global division of labor while framing normal supply relationships as risks and seeking to sever industrial chains. Meanwhile, there is no such thing as a shortcut in the global critical mineral industrial chain. The formation of a mature industrial system is the long-term combined result of resource endowment, technology accumulation, market scale and cost structure. It cannot be completely rearranged by a few technological breakthroughs or several policy measures. China's rare-earth export measures are fully reasonable and compliant and have long provided stable, reliable supplies for related industries across the world. By hyping "reducing dependence on China," some economies appear to be pursuing supply chain security; in reality they are narrowing their own path of development. Supply chain security can never be achieved through artificial fragmentation. Overall, recycling rare-earth metals from old wind turbines is a worthwhile pursuit within the circular economy, but it should be judged as a supplementary industrial strategy - not burdened with geopolitical expectations.
